newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton mixed on new crop arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton mixed on new crop arrivals.

text.p: Gujarat cotton suffered a fresh setback while Punjab varieties remained steady at the lower level on the cotton market on Thursday, dealers said.
"Gujarat varieties attracted fresh offerings by stockists on reports of rising new crop arrivals in the Gujarat region," one dealer said.

In spot deals Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) moved down to 19,500/20,400 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) from 20,000/20,500 rupees. Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) also slid by 300/500 rupees to 13,200/13,500 rupees per candy. Punjab cotton remained steady at the lower level amid limited activity.
Punjab saw-ginned remained steady at 1,580/1,700 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) for the average variety and at 1,750/1,800 rupees per maund for the superior variety.
Bengal-deshi was quiet at 870/890 rupees per maund.
